story.title: Customer profile: add preferred name and secondary email
story.description: Extend the customer profile with an optional preferred name and secondary email for service notifications. The customer-service stores this personal data in customer-db through a backward-compatible schema change and synchronizes the contact projection with CRM. The notification-service may use the secondary email only after verification and explicit customer consent. Keep the legal name and primary email behavior unchanged, including customers who leave the new fields blank. Apply existing retention, access, correction and erasure controls to both fields, and record the consent evidence needed for GDPR review.
acceptance_criteria: Preferred name accepts 1-80 characters and is optional; the legal name remains unchanged.
Secondary email must have valid email syntax and complete verification before notification delivery is enabled.
Customer profile updates persist in customer-db and synchronize with CRM without overwriting the primary email.
Withdrawal of consent stops secondary email notifications, and access or erasure requests include both new personal data fields.

requirement.business_summary: Add optional preferred name and secondary email fields to the customer profile for personalized service notifications, with verification and consent controls while preserving existing legal name and primary email behavior.
requirement.technical_summary: Extend customer-service and customer-db with optional preferred_name (1-80 chars) and secondary_email fields, including verification and consent flags; update notification-service to check verification and consent before using the secondary email; synchronize changes to CRM contact projection; apply existing retention, access, correction, and erasure controls to the new fields; record consent evidence for GDPR compliance.
requirement.engineering_scope: Add fields to customer-service and customer-db schema, update notification-service logic for verification and consent, synchronize with CRM contact projection, and apply existing data governance controls.

tests.title: Setting secondary email with verification and consent creates audit event recording consent evidence
steps: 1. Authenticate a test customer via /auth/token.
2. PATCH /customers/{id}/profile with {"preferred_name":"Johnny","secondary_email":"johnny@example.com","verification_pending":true,"consent":true}.
3. Simulate email verification by calling POST /customers/{id}/emails/verification with a valid test token.
4. Wait for eventual consistency.
5. Query audit-db for events where customer_id = {id} and event_type = "secondary_email_consent".
6. Verify that exactly one such event exists with consent=true and timestamp within the test window.
tests.expected: Audit DB contains a consent evidence event recording the secondary email consent.

tests.title: Verified secondary email influences fraud engine risk score when consented
steps: 1. Create a customer with no secondary email.
2. Perform a small payment transaction via POST /payments.
3. Call the fraud screening endpoint to obtain a baseline risk score.
4. Add a secondary email via PATCH profile with verification_pending false, consent false.
5. Verify the email via the verification endpoint.
6. Set consent true via PATCH profile.
7. Repeat the same payment transaction.
8. Obtain the fraud risk score after the transaction.
9. Verify that the risk score differs from the baseline (e.g., decreased by at least 5 points) due to the additional verified contact.
tests.expected: Fraud engine risk score updates reflecting the verified secondary email.

tests.title: Loan service uses preferred name in email notifications when secondary email verified and consented
steps: 1. Set preferred name "Liz" and a verified, consented secondary email via PATCH and verification endpoints.
2. Submit a loan application via POST /loans/applications.
3. Upon approval (simulate or trigger), the notification-service sends an email to the secondary email.
4. Intercept the email (test harness) and verify the body contains a greeting "Dear Liz" and the secondary email address.
tests.expected: Loan service communication uses the preferred name and is sent to the verified secondary email.

tests.summary: Selected 15 catalog tests and 8 new tests, covering 17 of 19 impacted nodes (89%); estimated effort is 13.2 hours.

frameworks.reason: PII-bearing components are impacted; the change touches customer data.

findings.text: The change adds preferred_name and secondary_email fields to the customer profile system of record, expanding the personal data held in customer-service and customer-db. Exposure to be assessed against purpose limitation, data minimization, retention and erasure expectations for the new fields.

Verification and consent flags used by notification-service introduce a new processing purpose for secondary email contact data, and consent evidence handling needs to be confirmed before the field is used for notifications.

Synchronizing the new fields into the CRM contact projection extends the population of records in scope for access, correction, erasure and consent-withdrawal handling downstream of the system of record.
Profile reads traverse api-gateway and authentication-service, so fields returned by existing profile paths should be confirmed as appropriately scoped for each calling channel and service.

recommendations: Confirm lawful basis, stated purpose, retention and erasure handling for preferred_name and secondary_email across customer-service, customer-db, crm and notification-service.
Verify consent capture, evidence retention and withdrawal propagation before notification-service is permitted to use the secondary email, including preferences surfacing through crm.
Review profile read paths through api-gateway and authentication-service to confirm the new fields are scoped, minimized or masked appropriately for each caller.
Confirm subject access, correction and erasure flows cover the new fields and that audit-db logging for profile changes is consistent with existing retention controls.

findings.text: The change does not touch card data directly, but card-service shares customer-db, api-gateway and authentication-service with the profile flow, so the exposure is whether new profile fields can enter card-data request or response paths.
Identity and gateway paths carry both card and profile traffic; ignored or widened token scope, masking or step-up behavior on these shared components would be the exposure area requiring check.
New profile change events will be written alongside cardholder-related access records in audit-db, so integrity, append-only behavior and retention consistency require confirmation.

recommendations: Confirm no cardholder data fields or card-service payloads are extended by the profile change, and verify masking remains enforced in card-service and api-gateway responses.
Verify authentication-service token scopes and step-up checks still gate card status and replacement actions after the change.
Review audit-db capture to confirm cardholder-data access records remain complete and unchanged in scope alongside new profile events.

frameworks.reason: financial-data components are impacted; audit-data components are impacted.

findings.text: Financial data is not directly touched, but customer-db and audit-db are shared with account-service and payment-service flows; the exposure is whether schema changes affect keys, joins or audit queries relied on for financial reporting.
Audit-db is an append-only store with integrity and retention controls, so new profile change events should be confirmed as not affecting the immutability or queryability of financial audit records.
A database schema change to a tier1 record store is subject to change-management evidence expectations, including approval, testing and rollback documentation.

recommendations: Verify the customer-db schema change remains backward-compatible with account-service, payment-service, loan-service and reporting reads and does not alter financial reconciliation joins.
Confirm change-management approval, testing and rollback evidence is recorded for the customer-service and customer-db changes.
Review audit-db to confirm new profile change events are appended without altering the integrity or completeness of financial audit queries.

findings.text: The change modifies highly critical tier1 core components that act as the customer profile system of record, so service-owner approval and rollback planning for customer-service and customer-db require confirmation.

Behavior changes in notification-service and synchronized CRM contact projection cross team ownership boundaries, exposing interface review and coordination expectations between Customer Platform and downstream consumers.

Multiple dependents read from customer-db, including account-service, loan-service, card-service and authentication-service, so schema or projection changes carry regression exposure for those consumers.

recommendations: Obtain service-owner approval and record the rollback plan for customer-service and customer-db before release.
Verify interface and behavior review with crm and notification-service owners, covering verification and consent handling for the secondary email.
Confirm regression, authorization and monitoring evidence for customer-db dependents including account-service, loan-service, card-service and authentication-service.
Record release evidence and operational monitoring expectations for the affected customer-platform components.
